# Workout Plan Page

← [Hub: skills.md](../skills.md) · Status: **Built (M6)**: plan generation, weekly view, swaps, coverage, body weight (part 1); core lifts, 6-week blocks, progressive overload and changes with preview (part 2)

**Purpose:** the person's weekly customised workout plan, generated by the LLM, which the person can change. Today's part of it appears on [Plan for Today](plan-for-today.md).

## Requirements

1. **Weekly customised workout plan.** The person can add or change something (e.g. add a session, swap an exercise, mark a day unavailable). If that change affects the rest of the week, the plan automatically rebalances.
2. **Body weight input** saved to the backend (feeds the opt-in weight card on the [Summary](summary.md)). Weight lifted per exercise is logged separately (see progressive overload below).
3. **Explanation of the plan:** what type of workout each session is and which muscles it targets.

## Session structure

Every workout follows these five phases, in this order, and every activity is labelled with its phase (here and on [Plan for Today](plan-for-today.md)):

1. **Cardio:** at the beginning, to warm up.
2. **Mobility:** for the joints used in that day's session.
3. **Activation:** of the muscles targeted that day.
4. **Main workout.**
5. **Cooldown and stretching.**

## Features

- **Effort feedback:** after each session, a quick "how hard was it?" (easy / right / too hard) that the next plan uses.
- **Exercise swaps:** alternatives from the same phase that hit the same muscles with the available equipment.
- **Preview before changing the week:** when a change rebalances the plan, show what moves (e.g. "Leg day moves from Wed to Fri") and apply it only after the person confirms.
- **Progressive overload:** sets, reps and weight lifted are logged per exercise; next week's plan adjusts the load from what was actually done. Shown over time as load capacity on [Progress](progress.md).
- **Weekly muscle coverage:** a body map or table showing sets per muscle group for the week, so gaps and imbalances are visible.

## Plan inputs

For each person (set on [Settings / Profile](settings-profile.md)): available days, time per session, equipment, training location (home / gym / travel), plus confirmed facts from [Personal Artifacts](personal-artifacts.md).

## Out of scope

- **75 Hard:** Amol's two daily workouts are ticked off on the [75 Hard](75-hard.md) checklist, not planned here.
- **Parked suggestions (not selected):** "why this plan" note, missed-workout rescheduling, deload weeks, plan history.

## As built (M6 part 1)

**When plans are made.** Opening the app in a week with no plan makes one (for your own profile; one shared request, so it's never made twice). **Make a new plan** makes another; when a plan already exists, the new one is a **preview** ("New plan ready to preview", with what changes per day) and replaces the current one only on **Use this plan** (or is dropped with **Keep current plan**). A plan made mid-week starts from today.

**How a plan is made** (`backend/core/workouts/`):

1. **Rules** set the shape: training days from Settings (from today on; at most 6, keeping a rest day); split by number of days (1–3 full body, 4 upper/lower, 5 upper/lower/push/pull/legs, 6 push/pull/legs twice); minutes per phase (cardio 12% of the session, 20% for fat loss or endurance; mobility and cooldown larger for the mobility goal); defaults for sets, reps and rest by goal and experience (strength 4×4–6 / beginners 3×6–8; muscle 4×8–12 / 3×8–12; fat loss or endurance 3×12–15; otherwise 3×8–12).
2. **Only doable exercises**: the person's equipment (Settings → library equipment), pull-up bar and bench checked by name, experience level (beginner: beginner exercises; intermediate: no expert ones; olympic lifts and strongman only for advanced). Gym = full gym.
3. **Warm-up and cool-down by rules**: cardio is the person's machine for the whole cardio time, or (no machine) rounds of three one-minute bodyweight drills; mobility uses moving stretches (circles, swings, lunges); activation is two light bodyweight/band moves (holds timed, 30 s); cooldown uses held stretches (45 s). All matched to the day's muscles.
4. **The LLM picks the main exercises** from a short list per day (about 14, compound first, matched to the day's muscles, varied across the week), and sets sets/reps/rest, respecting the injury notes; it writes each session's title and one-sentence explanation and a short rationale for the week. The answer is compact (Groq's free tier allows 1,000 output tokens a minute) and checked: exercises must come from that day's list, 2 to count+1 of them, sensible numbers; a session that fails the check uses the rules' picks.
5. **Where**: straight away on Vercel with Groq (up to 25 s). If Groq is slow, over its per-minute limit, or not set up, the job `generate_workout_plan` goes to the Mac worker (Groq, then Ollama, then rules alone), and the page shows "Making this week's plan…" until it's ready.

**The page** (`/workout-plan`): week dates; the week's rationale; each day Monday–Sunday (rest days shown as Rest); a training day opens to its five phases with each exercise (linking to the Exercise Guide) and its prescription ("3 × 8–12 · rest 90 s", "2 × 1 min", "45 s"); today's day starts open. **Swap** on main and activation exercises lists up to 6 alternatives (same phase, sharing a primary muscle, the person's equipment and level, not already in that session; same kind of movement first). **Muscles this week**: body map (dark red 6+ sets, light red 1–5), sets per muscle as bars, and major muscles with no sets. Body weight input at the bottom. On the other person's profile everything is view-only and drafts aren't shown.

## As built (M6 part 2)

**Core lifts.** Each person chooses up to 8 core lifts in Settings → Training (only big compound lifts they can do with their saved equipment and level are offered). Core lifts are in every plan, first in the main workout, each in up to 2 sessions a week (not on back-to-back days) whose focus trains its muscles, so their weights can keep going up. A chosen core lift that can't be done (equipment, level) is left out and the week's rationale says so.

**6-week blocks.** Other main exercises stay the same for 6 weeks: a new week copies last week's non-core main exercises by session type (only new kinds of session ask the LLM), and the rationale shows "Week N of 6 of this block". After 6 weeks, or with **Make a new plan**, a new block starts with fresh picks. Plans record `block_start`.

**Progressive overload** (`backend/core/workouts/overload.py`), from the most recent logged session of each main exercise and that session's effort rating:

- Weighted: every set at the top of the rep range (or rated **easy** with every set in range) → one step heavier (barbell, machine, cable 2.5 kg; dumbbell 2 kg; kettlebell 4 kg); most sets below the range → one step lighter; rated **too hard** → same weight; otherwise same weight, aim for more reps.
- Bodyweight and bands: every set at the top → rep range up by 2 (to 30 at most).
- Each target comes with a note, e.g. "Last time 3×12 at 20 kg: try 22 kg."

**Changes** (Workout Plan → **Change this week**), each shown as a preview ("For: …") and applied only with **Use this plan**; **Keep current plan** drops the change. Days already done this week (and today, once started) are kept as they are, and logged sets and completions move to the new plan.

| Change | What it does |
|---|---|
| Can't train on a day | That day becomes rest; the rest of the week rebalances (e.g. 4 days upper/lower → 3 full body). |
| Add a session | An extra training day this week; the split is recalculated. |
| Less time on a day | That session's minutes (phases shrink to fit). |
| Vacation | Dates, then **No training** (days off) or **Short bodyweight sessions** (bodyweight and bands only). Remembered for later weeks. |
| Cheat meal day | Always asks: **Spread the extra load across the week** (about 30 extra cardio minutes over the following sessions, at most 10 a day; never one "burn it off" session) or **Keep workouts as planned** (just saved, for the Nutrition Plan in M7). |
| Medical emergency | Training pauses from that day, until an end date or **I'm back**; the first week back is lighter (a set fewer, about 15% lighter). The form reminds to follow medical advice. |
| Something else | Free text, e.g. "knee hurts, nothing heavy for legs": the LLM turns it into days off, shorter days, muscles to avoid and/or an easier week for the rest of this week; if it can't, the person is asked to pick a specific change. |

A change for a later week (e.g. next week's vacation) is saved straight away and shapes that week's plan when it's made. Applied changes are listed under "Changes this week".
